archetype: Aggro, and the frame agrees. deck-audit reads the archetype off strategic_frame.json as aggro and the deck answers to it: 29 creatures inside the 26-32 band, modal mana value 2, threat-density 13 against a floor of 3. The more precise name is a linear go-wide typal deck — Edgar's eminence is the ignition and every cheap Vampire is a two-for-one — with an aristocrats drain package bolted to the side. The pilot has just unbolted it.
verdict: This deck functions and develops: 91.6% turn-3 land drops, 81.7% of first sevens kept, a modal mana value of 2, and a lord package that assembles 77.2% of games. What limits it is conversion, and the axis that shows it is interaction — 12 removal copies against an aggro target of 5-6, in a deck whose only card that turns board width into damage without attacking is Purphoros, and whose only checker-passed kills rest on Exquisite Blood. Refill is the second problem and it is smaller than the counted 3 suggests: Welcoming Vampire, Vanquisher's Banner, Minas Tirith and Preacher of the Schism all scale with the board, and two of those four are outside the count.

axes.reading: Three counted draw pieces — Night's Whisper, Vanquisher's Banner, Welcoming Vampire — against a template of 10. The audit's probe list is not the one-shot life payment this artifact previously called it: Minas Tirith and Castle Locthwain are repeatable activated draws, Preacher of the Schism draws on attack, and Midgar's adventure half draws two. Six or seven functions, most of them board-gated and slow. Real, and under target — but the gap is not 3 against 10.

engine.declared: Edgar's eminence turns every Vampire cast into a body, doublers turn that body into four, lords turn four 1/1s into a lethal board, and a small package converts board width into each-opponent life loss without anything having to die.

components.reading: The one component that never fails to assemble: eminence works from the command zone, so the ignition is available every game from turn one. This is why the deck's problem is never 'do I have the engine' — it is what the engine is pointed at.

Eight lords and pump effects, assembling 77.2% of games at a mean turn of 2.74. This is the deck's best-built component and deck_recon.json confirms the deck runs every lord the community treats as non-negotiable. Leave it alone.

The token amplifiers — the component the pilot's direction says IS the deck — are four cards assembling 52.1% of games, the thinnest on-direction group in the deck. Two are true doublers; Ocelot Pride makes Cats, not Vampires, and Mavren Fein needs an attack first. The measured rate is also deflated: goldfish_targets.json names 'Bloodline Keeper' while the maindeck card is 'Bloodline Keeper // Lord of Lineage', so the simulation never counted a fifth member.

The width payoff that needs no combat is exactly one card. Stack 008 verified it at 10 damage to each opponent per two-mana Vampire cast through both doublers — five triggers at 2, the highest-leverage measured line in the deck — and there is no second copy of the effect. goldfish_targets.json does not declare this component at all.

The width-drain half of the drain package, and it is not the aristocrats half: Sanctum Seeker pays on attacks, Throne on tapped creatures, Bloodletter doubles both, Twilight Prophet on ten permanents. Stacks 003 and 007 measure it. The pilot's direction does not touch these — nothing has to die.

components.reading: goldfish_targets.json declares this as "The two-piece infinite assembled (a lose-half + a gain-half)" — an AND over two two-card pairs, [Vito, Sanguine Bond] and [Exquisite Blood, Bloodthirsty Conqueror] — and the 9.4% is measured on exactly that membership. Cruel Celebrant appears in no declared component at all. Exquisite Blood's departure deletes one of the two gain-halves, so the 9.4% describes a set the deck will not have; stacks 001 and 005 both rest on it and are orphaned by the move regardless of anything here.
Five, assembling 60.9%. Two of them are typal cost reduction rather than acceleration, which is the right shape for this deck and the reason the ramp axis reads worse than the deck plays.

Six, assembling 68.0%. Four of the six — Akroma's Will, Boros Charm, Flawless Maneuver, Teferi's Protection — protect the whole board at instant speed. Deflecting Swat retargets one spell or ability and cannot answer an untargeted wrath; Swiftfoot Boots covers one creature. These six are the deck's whole protection budget and they are in band.

The declared draw group assembles 61.5%, but Black Market Connections is leaving and Night's Whisper is one card at sorcery speed. Two of the four that remain do scale with width: Welcoming Vampire draws "whenever one or more other creatures you control with power 2 or less enter", which is every 1/1 Vampire token, and Preacher of the Schism draws on attack. What none of them is, is a rebuild after the board is gone.

cut_candidates.why: A symmetric sweeper in the widest deck at the table. The deck runs 29 creatures and manufactures more every cast; paying X life to give all creatures -X/-X kills more of yours than anyone's, and against a token board it is the opponents' best card, not yours. Olivia's Wrath already covers the slot and spares Vampires by construction, which keeps the sweeper axis inside its 1-3 band.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: The format's premier scalable answer, and the only sweeper in the deck that scales to any toughness and hits everything — Olivia's Wrath also beats indestructible (zero toughness does) and targets nothing, but it spares Vampires and is capped at your own Vampire count, and the five exile effects answer one permanent each. What is unique to the Deluge is the "at any size" clause on a sweeper. Cutting it means the deck genuinely cannot answer a board it cannot race, and it is EDHREC rank 67 for that reason. Recommending it anyway because a sweeper you cannot cast is a slot, not an answer — and I re-ran deck-audit on the post-departure list with the Deluge removed: sweepers reads 1, still inside the 1-3 band.

open_questions.question: goldfish_targets.json declares a seven-card 'Drain engine' and a two-piece infinite as first-class components while declaring the token amplifiers as four cards, and it declares no component at all for the width payoff (Purphoros). With Exquisite Blood gone, should the targets be re-derived around the width plan — amplifiers, non-eminence token makers, width payoffs, refill — rather than around the drain?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The engine block is read straight from that file, so every assembly rate in this diagnosis is measuring the old deck's intent. Until the targets are re-derived, the audit will keep reporting the deck's best-assembling component as a drain package the pilot is dismantling, and will keep not measuring the thing the pilot says the deck is.

open_questions.question: goldfish_targets.json names 'Bloodline Keeper' in the Token amplifier group, but the maindeck card is 'Bloodline Keeper // Lord of Lineage'. `manamap pilot impact` flags it as a name not in the maindeck with rates silently deflated. What is the amplifier group's rate with the fifth member counted?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 52.1% figure is the number this diagnosis calls the deck's thinnest on-direction component, and it is measured off four cards when five are in the deck. Fixing the name is a one-line change; the corrected rate could move the amplifier group from thinnest to adequate and would change how many of the amplifier adds are worth taking.

open_questions.question: Warleader's Call resolving alongside Purphoros through Anointed Procession and Mondrak: how much damage does one two-mana Vampire cast actually deal, and does the anthem's +1/+1 apply to the tokens created by the same eminence trigger?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 008 verified 10 damage to each opponent per two-mana Vampire from Purphoros alone — four token triggers plus the creature's own entry, five triggers at 2. If the second pinger stacks cleanly the deck has a measured non-combat kill with redundancy on both halves — which is the difference between a token deck and a token deck that wins. Nothing about this line is verified and it must not be presented as fact until it is.

open_questions.question: Reconnaissance in this shell: can Edgar's attack trigger and Sanctum Seeker's attack drain both be banked and the team then removed from combat before blockers, as PapLaRiviere's primer claims?
open_questions.why_it_matters: deck_recon.json records this as a one-source claim about a one-mana white enchantment built for exactly this attack-trigger shell, and this repo has verified nothing about it. If it holds, it is a one-mana answer to both the deck's problems at once — it converts attacking into a free action and it keeps the board off the wrath. If it does not, a cheap card gets recommended on a primer's say-so.

open_questions.question: Does a go-wide Edgar actually lose to sweepers, or to spot removal on the lords?
open_questions.why_it_matters: deck_recon.json names this as a gap it could not close: Gregory asserts lords-eat-removal and the answer is +1/+1 counters, PapLaRiviere asserts hold-protection-for-the-wrath, and both are qualitative. This diagnosis now reads six dedicated protection slots, four of them board-wide, and leaves all six alone. If the first is right, two protection slots should have become counter-anthems instead, and the prescription changes shape.

open_questions.question: goldfish_targets.json's "Draw engine" group is Black Market Connections, Twilight Prophet, Welcoming Vampire, Preacher of the Schism and Night's Whisper. Black Market Connections is leaving, and three of the deck's actual draw functions are outside the group — Vanquisher's Banner, Minas Tirith and Castle Locthwain. What does refill assemble at when the component is declared over the cards the deck really draws with?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This pass downgraded card-advantage from liability to weakness on the oracle text alone, and the 61.5% is measured on a set about to be wrong in both directions. Whether refill is a real hole or a taxonomy artefact is a measurement nobody has taken, and it decides how many of the three draw adds are worth their slots.

gaps: The colour-sources figure of -11 is a floor, and this diagnosis could not compute the true one. `manabase.land_colors` scores Arid Mesa, Bloodstained Mire, Marsh Flats, Prismatic Vista, Reflecting Pool and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth at zero coloured sources each; all six really do produce black in play, and Urborg makes every land a black source. Black's real count is materially above 25 and the 71.8% on-curve figure is correspondingly pessimistic. Settling it needs a source model that resolves fetches and land-type changers.

This diagnosis was computed against a decklist that still contains Exquisite Blood, Grave Pact, Black Market Connections and Agadeem's Awakening. Every axis figure carries the audit's number for that 100-card list, as the contract requires. Rather than assert the consequences, I re-ran deck-audit on the post-departure list: mana-base stays 37 (Agadeem is a Sorcery // Land and was never counted), ramp falls 7 to 5, interaction 12 to 11, threat-density 13 to 12, colour-sources -11 to -12, and card-advantage stays 3 (Black Market Connections was never in the count either). Those runs are views, not artifacts; the tracked figures stay as the audit computes them today.

Stacks 001 and 005 both name Exquisite Blood in their scenarios and are orphaned by the departure, independently of anything recommended here. The deck's verified-line count drops from eight to six on the day the cards leave, and nothing in this diagnosis restores it. The three lines that measure the width plan — 002, 003, 007, 008 — are untouched.

No verified line exists for the token plan's kill. Stacks 002, 003, 007 and 008 measure tokens per cast, drain per attack, drain per end step and damage per cast; none of them is a scenario in which the deck wins. The deck's only checker-passed kills were the Exquisite Blood loops, and they are leaving.

Ownership was deliberately not used as a ranking input, per the pilot's note that the spare Vampire cards are not yet catalogued. Ten of the ten adds are ranked on what the deck needs; two (Charismatic Conqueror, Cemetery Gatekeeper) are known to be on hand because they are in the sideboard, and the other eight are acquisition questions this artifact does not answer.

Findings that lean on deck_recon.json (as_of 2026-08-03) are dated meta claims and will expire: the Champion of Dusk, Caretaker's Talent, Charismatic Conqueror, Warleader's Call, Elspeth, Patchwork Banner, Pact of the Serpent and Malakir Bloodwitch entries all cite an inclusion rate or an article. The construction principles they sit under do not expire; the percentages do.

deck_recon.json's own gap stands and this diagnosis inherits it: no fetchable primer exists for a genuinely graveyard-free, drain-free Edgar. Every published go-wide list still runs Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant or a sac outlet, so the prescription here is the archetype minus the parts the pilot excluded, not a copy of a list someone has proven.

Three Tree City is the one typal land this repo cannot price, and the previous pass dismissed it wrongly. manabase.land_colors scores it zero because the parser finds no colour symbol and its colour identity is empty — not because its mana is restricted: "{2}, {T}: Choose a color. Add an amount of mana of that color equal to the number of creatures you control of the chosen type" carries no spend restriction at all, and it scales with the tokens this deck manufactures. Against that, it taps for {C} until you pay {2}, which is the wrong shape for a modal-mana-value-2 curve. Settling it needs a source model that prices creature-count-scaled lands; it is not prescribed here.

The previous pass reported 16 taplands and had to argue the figure down by hand, because manabase.enters_tapped is a substring superset that counts "enters tapped unless" lands as tapped. deck-audit now separates them natively — 3 unconditional, 13 conditional_or_shock — so that gap is closed and the axis is re-derived from the tool. What is still unmeasured is a turn-indexed untapped-source count: nothing here says how often the deck has the right two or three colours untapped on turn two, which is the only question the conditional thirteen still raise.

Command Tower is withdrawn, not refuted. The previous pass prescribed it to close taplands when that axis read 16; it reads 3 against a cap of 8 and is in band, and the swap it rested on — Nomad Outpost, one of the three unconditional taplands, for an untapped land of the same three colours — is land-count-neutral and colour-neutral, so it moves taplands from 3 to 2 and no other axis at all. That is a free swap, not a fix, and an add that closes nothing measured is a preference. The straight-add version was the colour argument, and gaps[0] takes it apart: black's real source count is materially above the 25 the tool sees, and the add would push a 37-land aggro deck to 38, further over its 34-36 band. Recon's 94.4% inclusion rate in Tokens-tagged Edgar lists is a fact about other decks, not a reason here.
